title: the orient floor writes forward-slash refs on every box
intention: Every repo-relative ref the orient floor writes into a chart packet is spelled with forward slashes, whichever box drafted it.
why: Measured 2026-11-13 by the orchestrator: a9709b744bf5's orient, drafted on akiendell, was refused on Linux with 'refs the floor cannot verify exist: cairn\devices\cairn, cairn\devices\codemother, cairn\devices\codemother\machines\clearance, cairn\machines\learning_block'. Read on akienasus the same day: floor_packet builds those refs from component_home and _repo_relative, and both are os.path.relpath. 033f607c5316 fixed cairn/tools/orient (89973002c), not this floor.
traces_to: Law 8 (a packet reads the same on every box); outline 5.5.3.8.
how: D1 posixes at the write in floor_packet; D2 proves it with Windows simulated on Linux.

clauses.claim: floor_packet, fed component homes and relpaths spelled with backslashes, stores refs with no backslash, and its domain names their rungs
orient's every_ref_exists inspection, run on Linux over those refs, finds none invented

decisions.text: D1: floor_packet writes each in-repo ref (from _repo_relative and component_home) with every backslash turned into '/', so refs and the domain derived from them read the same on every box. A ref outside the repo is kept exactly as the request wrote it.

D2: the proof simulates Windows on Linux. It patches orient's component_home and os.path.relpath to return backslash paths, then restores both. Tooth 1 asserts the stored refs carry no backslash and the domain names their rungs. Tooth 2 runs orient's every_ref_exists inspection over those refs and finds none invented.

measured.saw: floor_packet's in-repo refs come from component_home (os.path.relpath) and _repo_relative (os.path.relpath); _rung splits on '/'
